mainTopic: The special קרבנות of the כהן משיח and the נשיא: sins committed after leaving office or before being appointed, who counts as a נשיא, and the idea that leadership is servitude.
overview: The גמרא first explains why the משנה bothers to say that a כהן משיח who sinned and then left office brings a פר: the line is there to contrast him with the נשיא. Two ברייתות then show that the משיח keeps his פר after leaving office ("וְהִקְרִיב עַל חַטָּאתוֹ"), while the נשיא does not ("אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא"). In each case a פסוק overrides a קל וחומר. A new משנה rules that a king or כהן משיח who sinned before being appointed is treated like a הדיוט, though רבי שמעון makes it depend on when he found out about the sin. The same משנה defines the נשיא as the king, who has only ה׳ above him. The גמרא shows that each leader needs his own פסוק to exclude earlier sins, because each is "stronger" in a different way, so a קל וחומר fails in both directions. A ברייתא explains that "אֲשֶׁר" does not mean the king is fated to sin. This leads to a side discussion of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון on נגעים, where רבא and רב פפא narrow רבי שמעון's exclusion. The amud then shows that a king struck with צרעת is removed from office, and learns from "בֵּית הַחׇפְשִׁית" that ruling is a kind of servitude. It ends with the story of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע on a ship, which leads רבן גמליאל to appoint two poor scholars. The story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why say the obvious case of the anointed priest?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a משיח who left office and then sinned still brings a פר. The גמרא asks why the משנה also needs the easier case of one who sinned first and left office afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and afterward sinned, he brings a bull. If he sinned first and only afterward left his anointed position, does that need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה's case of a משיח who left office and then sinned, who still brings a פר. Then it asks why the משנה also bothers to teach the case where he sinned while still in office.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a משיח brings a פר even for a sin done after leaving office, then he surely brings one for a sin done while he was in office. So that second case looks like it adds nothing. The question pushes the גמרא to find a reason for it.

keyTerms.meaning: the status of being the anointed כהן גדול
left or was removed from his position
does it need to be said? (meaning: it seems obvious)
a bull, the special חטאת of the כהן משיח

phrases.english: and afterward sinned, brings a bull.
If he sinned and afterward left his anointed position,
does that need to be said?

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that a משיח who sinned and then left office brings a פר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he brings a פר even for a sin after leaving office, then he surely brings one for a sin committed while in office. That makes the line seem unnecessary.

steps.title: It is taught to contrast with the king
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the משיח case so it can set it side by side with the נשיא, who loses his special קרבן once he leaves office.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה teaches about a king that when he left his kingship and afterward sinned he brings like a commoner, it therefore teaches about the anointed priest: if he sinned and afterward left office, he brings a bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משיח line is written as a matching pair to the נשיא line. The point is to show how the two differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נשיא who left office and then sinned brings the קרבן of a הדיוט. The משנה lines up the משיח cases next to the נשיא cases to make the contrast clear. The line is about presenting the cases side by side, not about adding a new law.

keyTerms.meaning: the king or ruler, who brings his own special חטאת
the status of being the נשיא

phrases.english: Because it teaches regarding a king
that when he left his kingship
and afterward sinned, he brings like a commoner,
therefore it teaches regarding the anointed priest:
[if he sinned and afterward left office,] he brings a bull.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, and they make clear which case is meant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the משנה's style: the line is a parallel set up to contrast with the נשיא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to add nothing, since the case looked obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is taught to match the נשיא case and show that the משיח keeps his פר where the נשיא does not.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a משיח who left office and then sinned still brings a פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. It is setting up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule being questioned is that a former משיח still brings a פר. This is surprising, because he is no longer the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a משיח who left office still brings a פר.

steps.title: The verse teaches he brings even after leaving office
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "וְהִקְרִיב עַל חַטָּאתוֹ" that the משיח brings his חטאת even after he left office.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: "And he shall offer for his sin" teaches that he brings his sin-offering even after he has left office.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words "עַל חַטָּאתוֹ", "for his sin", tie the קרבן to the person who sinned, not to the job he holds. So he brings the פר even after leaving office.

keyTerms.meaning: and he shall offer for his sin

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And he shall offer for his sin,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

phrases.english: teaches that he brings his sin-offering after he has left office.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "וְהִקְרִיב עַל חַטָּאתוֹ" teaches that he brings the פר even after leaving office.

steps.title: Logic would say the anointed priest loses his bull
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why the פסוק is needed. A קל וחומר from the נשיא would have taught that a former משיח does NOT bring a פר.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might think: is it not logical? If a king, who brings for an unwitting act alone, does not bring his sin-offering after he has left office, then an anointed priest, who does not bring for an unwitting act alone but only for a mistaken ruling together with an unwitting act, surely does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא builds a קל וחומר that would lead to the opposite rule. This shows why the פסוק was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נשיא brings his special חטאת for any accidental sin, so his קרבן applies more often. A משיח brings his פר only when he also gave a mistaken ruling, so his קרבן applies less often. If the broader קרבן of the נשיא ends when he leaves office, then the narrower one of the משיח should surely end too.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not logical? (opens a קל וחומר)
a mistaken ruling; not knowing what the law is

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר is NOT the conclusion. It is the wrong idea that the פסוק comes to block. The final rule is that the former משיח DOES bring a פר.

phrases.english: For one might think: is it not logical?
If a king, who brings for an unwitting act,
does not bring his sin-offering after he has left office,
then an anointed priest, who does not bring for an unwitting act

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.english: but only for a mistaken ruling together with an unwitting act,
is it [not] all the more so that he does not bring!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The point is that the משיח surely should NOT bring one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the פסוק in step 4 is needed by presenting the logic it overrides.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a former משיח still brings a פר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נשיא's קרבן is broader, and it ends when he leaves office. So the משיח's narrower קרבן should surely end too.

steps.title: The verse overrides the logic
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא repeats that "וְהִקְרִיב עַל חַטָּאתוֹ" teaches the משיח brings his חטאת even after leaving office, despite the קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: "And he shall offer for his sin," teaching that he brings for his sin even after he has left office.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר with the פסוק, which sets the law against that logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone would have taken the פר away from a former משיח. The פסוק shows that his obligation stays with him. When a פסוק is clear, it overrides a קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן משיח keeps his פר obligation even after he leaves office. This comes from "וְהִקְרִיב עַל חַטָּאתוֹ", even though a קל וחומר pointed the other way.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "And he shall offer for his sin,"
teaching that he brings for his sin even after he has left office.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קל וחומר of step 5 by bringing the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A former משיח should not bring a פר, by קל וחומר from the נשיא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He does bring a פר after leaving office, because of the פסוק.

steps.title: Then the king should also keep his offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the logic around. If the משיח keeps his קרבן after leaving office, the נשיא should keep his too, by קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let a king also bring, through a קל וחומר: if an anointed priest, who does not bring for an unwitting act alone, brings a sin-offering after he has left office, then a king, who does bring a sin-offering for an unwitting act, should surely bring his sin-offering after he has left office!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that a former נשיא brings like a הדיוט. Now that we know the משיח keeps his קרבן, it uses that to build a קל וחומר for the נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite direction from step 5. The משיח, whose קרבן is narrower, keeps it after leaving office. So the נשיא, whose קרבן is broader, should surely keep his.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: But let a king also bring, through a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁאֵין מֵבִיא בְּשִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה
phrases.english: If an anointed priest, who does not bring for an unwitting act,
brings a sin-offering after he has left office,
then a king, who brings a sin-offering for an unwitting act,
is it not logical that he brings his sin-offering after he has left office!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 6 to challenge the נשיא rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that a נשיא who left office and then sinned brings like a הדיוט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משיח with his narrower קרבן keeps it, the נשיא with his broader קרבן should surely keep his.

steps.title: The verse limits the king to while he reigns
steps.stepSummary: The words "אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא" teach that a נשיא brings his special קרבן only for sins he commits while he is still king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "When a king sins". When he is king, yes; when he is a commoner, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר with a פסוק that ties the נשיא's קרבן to his being king at the time of the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls him "נשיא" at the moment he sins. If he is already a הדיוט when he sins, he brings the קרבן of a הדיוט. The פסוק blocks the קל וחומר, so the משנה's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The משיח keeps his פר after leaving office ("וְהִקְרִיב עַל חַטָּאתוֹ"). The נשיא brings his special קרבן only while he is king ("אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא"). In each case the פסוק decides, not the קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the contrast in the משנה between the two leaders. Each one's law comes from the wording of his own פסוק.

phrases.english: The verse says: "When a king sins"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22

phrases.english: When he is king, yes;
when he is a commoner, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קל וחומר of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק overrides the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A former נשיא should keep his special קרבן, by קל וחומר from the משיח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק limits his special קרבן to sins committed while he is king. After that, he brings like a הדיוט.

steps.title: Sins committed before being appointed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a king or כהן משיח who sinned before his appointment is treated like a regular person. רבי שמעון makes it depend on when he found out about the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they sinned before they were appointed and were appointed afterward, they are like regular people. רבי שמעון says: if they found out about the sin before they were appointed, they must bring a קרבן. If they found out after they were appointed, they bring nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It deals with a king or כהן משיח who sinned while he was still a regular person and only later got his high position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא looks at when the sin was done. Since it was done before the appointment, he brings the regular קרבן of an individual. רבי שמעון looks at when he found out about the sin. If he only found out after the appointment, he is completely פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: they were appointed (as king or כהן גדול)
it became known to them (they found out they had sinned)
exempt, they bring no קרבן at all

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון's פטור does not mean he brings the regular person's קרבן. It means he brings no קרבן at all.

phrases.english: MISHNA: If they sinned before they were appointed,
phrases.notes: "They" means the king and the כהן משיח, the two people the earlier משניות were talking about.

phrases.english: and afterward they were appointed,
these are like regular people.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם נוֹדַע לָהֶם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַנּוּ –
phrases.english: If it became known to them before they were appointed,
they are obligated (to bring a קרבן),
but if it became known once they were appointed, they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It moves from someone who left office (steps 4-8) to someone who sinned before he entered office.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, sins done before the appointment get the regular person's קרבן. According to רבי שמעון, it depends on when he found out: if before the appointment he is חייב, if after he is פטור.

steps.title: The נשיא is the king
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the נשיא of the פסוק as the king, because the פסוק describes someone who has only ה׳ above him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the נשיא? It is the king, as the פסוק says, "of all the commandments of ה׳ his God," meaning someone who has nobody over him except ה׳ his God.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines who the פסוק means by "נשיא" for the special goat קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "ה׳ אלהיו" (his God) are read as a hint: this person answers only to ה׳. Only the king has nobody above him, so a tribal leader or other official does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: the leader who brings a special goat as his חטאת
over him, above him in authority

phrases.english: Who is the נשיא? This is a king,
as it is said: "of all the commandments of ה׳ his God,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין עַל גַּבָּיו אֶלָּא ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו.
phrases.english: meaning one who has nobody over him except ה׳ his God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה continues with a definition of one of the people in its ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נשיא of the פסוק is the king, since only he has nobody above him except ה׳.

steps.title: Where does the rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that sins done before the appointment are treated like a regular person's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated its rule without a source. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches that sins done before the appointment do not get the special קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: from where are these things known? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these things known?
phrases.notes: "These things" is the משנה's first rule: sins done before the appointment are like a regular person's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that sins done before the appointment do not get the special קרבן.

steps.title: The פסוק excludes earlier sins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק "if the anointed כהן shall sin" that the משיח's special קרבן does not cover sins he did before he was appointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: "If the anointed כהן shall sin," this excludes the earlier sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the פסוק about the כהן משיח as leaving out sins from before his appointment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls him "the anointed כהן" as the one who sins. That means the sin must be done while he is already anointed. Sins from before that point, called "הקודמות," are not included in his special פר.

keyTerms.meaning: the anointed כהן, the כהן גדול
to exclude the earlier ones (sins done before the appointment)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"If the anointed priest shall sin (to bring guilt),"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: this excludes the earlier ones,
phrases.notes: He means sins done before he became כהן משיח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "הכהן המשיח יחטא" teach that the special פר covers only sins done while he is already משיח, not earlier ones.

steps.title: Why not learn it from the נשיא?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that the פסוק should not be needed, because a קל וחומר from the נשיא already shows that the משיח does not bring for earlier sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might say: isn't it logical? A נשיא brings his קרבן for any accidental action, yet he does not bring for earlier sins. The משיח brings only when a mistaken ruling came together with an accidental action. Surely he should not bring for earlier sins!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק is needed at all. It argues that a קל וחומר from the נשיא would already teach this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נשיא's קרבן is the broader one, since it applies to any accidental sinful action, and still it does not cover earlier sins. The משיח's קרבן is narrower, since it applies only to a mistaken ruling plus an action. So the narrower one should certainly not cover earlier sins, which would make the פסוק seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't it logical? (introduces a קל וחומר)
a law that was hidden from him, a mistaken ruling

steps.confusionAlert: This is the ברייתא arguing that the פסוק looks unnecessary, not the final law. The ברייתא will go on to explain why the פסוק is still needed.

phrases.english: For one might have said: isn't it logical?
If a נשיא, who brings his קרבן for an accidental action,
does not bring for the earlier sins,
then an anointed priest, who does not bring

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה –
phrases.english: except for a mistaken ruling together with an accidental action,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא עַל הַקּוֹדְמוֹת!
phrases.english: isn't it logical that he should not bring for the earlier sins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the פסוק quoted in step 12 is really needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק "אם הכהן המשיח יחטא" to exclude earlier sins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the נשיא's broader קרבן does not cover earlier sins, so the משיח's narrower קרבן certainly should not. That would make the פסוק unnecessary.

steps.title: The קל וחומר from the king is broken
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר. The נשיא is weaker, because once he leaves office he stops bringing his special קרבן. The משיח keeps bringing his special קרבן even after he leaves office, so maybe he also brings it for earlier sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: No! You can say this about a נשיא, because he does not bring his special חטאת once he has left office. Can you say the same about a משיח, who does bring his special חטאת even after he has left office? Since he brings it even after leaving office, maybe he should also bring it for sins from before his appointment?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר from step 13. It shows that the משיח and the נשיא are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed the משיח is the more limited case. But the משיח's special status actually reaches further than the נשיא's, because it stays with him even after he leaves office. So we might think it also reaches backward to sins from before his appointment.

keyTerms.meaning: after he has passed out of office (he has stepped down or been removed)
the earlier ones: sins done before he was appointed
"since it is so that": points to a feature that makes one case different from the other

steps.confusionAlert: The question "יָבִיא עַל הַקּוֹדְמוֹת?" is not the final law. It is only a possible line of reasoning that the פסוק will block in the next step.

phrases.english: No, if you said this about a king,
that is because he does not bring his special sin-offering once he has left office,
phrases.notes: After stepping down, a king who sins brings an ordinary person's קרבן, not a king's goat.

phrases.english: will you say the same about an anointed כהן,
who brings his special sin-offering even after leaving office?
Since he brings his special sin-offering even after leaving office,
perhaps he should bring it for sins done before his appointment?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the קל וחומר proposed in step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from the נשיא to the משיח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משיח's status continues after he leaves office, which the נשיא's does not. So the משיח is not the weaker case.

steps.title: So the פסוק is needed for the anointed כהן
steps.stepSummary: Because the קל וחומר fails, the פסוק "הַמָּשִׁיחַ יֶחֱטָא" is needed. It teaches that only a sin done while he is משיח gets the משיח's special קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says "if the anointed כהן shall sin." If he sinned while he was משיח, he brings the special קרבן. If he sinned while he was still a regular כהן, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא concludes that the פסוק is truly needed, since logic alone could not prove the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "הַמָּשִׁיחַ" describes him at the moment of the sin. So what counts is his status when he sinned, not his status when he brings the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: "the פסוק teaches": introduces the פסוק that settles the question
a regular person (here, a כהן not yet anointed)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule (step 9) that sins done before the appointment are judged like a regular person's.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "If the anointed כהן shall sin,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

phrases.english: if he sinned while he was anointed, he brings the special offering;
if he sinned while he was a regular person, he does not bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר is rejected, the ברייתא shows why the פסוק is needed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משיח's special קרבן applies only to sins done while he is משיח, and this is learned from the פסוק.

steps.title: A matching ברייתא about the king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a similar ברייתא about the נשיא. The פסוק "אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא" excludes sins done before he became king.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is also a ברייתא that says the same thing about a king: "When a king sins" comes to exclude sins done earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows a parallel teaching for the king. It sets up a new round of question and answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the משיח has his own פסוק, the נשיא has his own. Next, the ברייתא will ask why this פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: "and it was also taught": introduces a supporting ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא נָמֵי גַּבֵּי נָשִׂיא כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא:
phrases.english: And it was also taught about a king in the same way:
"When a king sins": this excludes sins done earlier,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא נָמֵי גַּבֵּי נָשִׂיא כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא for the נשיא after finishing the משיח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נשיא does not bring his special קרבן for sins done before he became king.

steps.title: Maybe a קל וחומר from the anointed כהן is enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the king's פסוק is not needed. If the משיח, whose status lasts even after he leaves office, does not bring for earlier sins, then surely the נשיא, whose status ends when he leaves, does not either.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: isn't this logical? If a משיח, who brings his special חטאת even after leaving office, does not bring it for earlier sins, then a נשיא, who does not bring his special חטאת after leaving office, should certainly not bring it for earlier sins!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the need for the king's פסוק by building a קל וחומר in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that the משיח's status is the stronger one. So if even the stronger status does not reach back to earlier sins, the weaker status of the נשיא should not reach back either.

keyTerms.meaning: "isn't it logical?": introduces a קל וחומר meant to make the פסוק seem unnecessary

phrases.english: For one might have thought: isn't it logical?
If an anointed כהן, who brings his special sin-offering even after leaving office,
does not bring it for earlier sins,
then a king, who does not bring his special sin-offering after leaving office,

phrases.aramaic: – אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא עַל הַקּוֹדְמוֹת?
phrases.english: isn't it logical that he should not bring it for earlier sins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the פסוק cited in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק "אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the משיח, whose status is the stronger one, would already teach the נשיא's rule.

steps.title: The king is stronger in a different way
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא breaks this קל וחומר too. The משיח brings his special קרבן only when he acted on a mistaken ruling. The נשיא brings his for a plain accidental act, so maybe he also brings it for earlier sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a משיח? He does not bring his special קרבן for a plain accidental act. Can you say the same about a נשיא, who does bring for a plain accidental act? Since he brings for a plain accidental act, maybe he should also bring for earlier sins?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finds a way in which the נשיא is stronger than the משיח, so the קל וחומר no longer works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משיח brings his bull only if he sinned because he ruled the law wrongly. A נשיא brings his goat for any accidental sin. Because the נשיא's קרבן covers more kinds of sins, we might think it also covers sins from before he became king.

keyTerms.meaning: an accidental act on its own, without a mistaken ruling behind it
"what about...?": points out a difference that breaks a comparison

steps.confusionAlert: Each person is "stronger" in a different way. The משיח keeps his status after leaving office. The נשיא brings for any accidental act. Because of this, neither case can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: What about an anointed כהן? He is different, since
he does not bring for an accidental act on its own,
will you say the same about a king, who does bring for an accidental act on its own?
Since he brings for an accidental act on its own,
perhaps he should bring for earlier sins?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמָשִׁיחַ שֶׁכֵּן אֵין מֵבִיא בְּשִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks the קל וחומר of step 17
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from the משיח to the נשיא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The נשיא brings for an accidental act on its own, but the משיח does not. So the נשיא is not simply the weaker case.

steps.title: So the פסוק is needed for the king
steps.stepSummary: Because the קל וחומר fails, the פסוק "אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא" is needed. It teaches that only a sin done while he is king gets the king's special קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says "when a king sins": this means he sinned while he was already king, and not that he sinned while he was still a regular person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא concludes that the king's rule must come from his own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes him as a נשיא at the moment of the sin. So sins from before he became king are treated like a regular person's sins.
steps.whatToRemember: Both the משיח and the נשיא need their own פסוק. Each one is stronger than the other in a different way, so a קל וחומר cannot work in either direction. Together the פסוקים are the source of the משנה's rule that sins done before the appointment are treated like a regular person's sins.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "When a king sins":
meaning he sinned while he is already king,
and not that he sinned while he was still a regular person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the קל וחומר is rejected, the ברייתא shows why the king's פסוק is needed
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A נשיא brings his special קרבן only for sins done while he is king. This is learned from his own פסוק, since logic alone cannot prove it.

steps.title: The king's sin is not a set decree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the word "אֲשֶׁר" in the נשיא's פסוק might suggest his sin is decreed. The word "אִם" in the משיח's פסוק shows it only means "if he sins."
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "When (אֲשֶׁר) a king sins." Could this mean it is a decree that he will sin? The פסוק says: "If the anointed כהן sins." Just as there it means "in case he sins," so too here it means "in case he sins."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the special wording of the נשיא's פסוק. It uses the משיח's פסוק to show the king is not fated to sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everywhere else the תורה says "if" someone sins, but for the king it says "אֲשֶׁר", which sounds like "when" he sins. The ברייתא compares it to the משיח's פסוק, which uses "אִם". It concludes that the king's פסוק also means only "in the event that he sins."

keyTerms.meaning: A set decree, something fixed to happen
In the event that he sins

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"When a king sins"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22. The word אֲשֶׁר sounds like "when", as if it will surely happen.

phrases.english: One might think it is a decree?
The verse states: "If the anointed Kohen sins"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

phrases.english: just as there it means "in the event that he sins"
so too here it means "in the event that he sins."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא, יָכוֹל גְּזֵרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the נשיא's פסוק from steps 16-19, but turns to a new word in it: אֲשֶׁר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא" means "if the king sins", like "אִם הַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ יֶחֱטָא". It is not a decree that he will sin.

steps.title: Where would the idea of a decree come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why anyone would think the פסוק means the king is fated to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: "One might think it is a decree." A decree? Where would such an idea come from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא and asks why anyone would think of a decree at all. It is setting up the next step, which will show where this idea comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא only uses "יָכוֹל" (one might think) for a reasonable mistake. The גמרא wants to know what makes it reasonable to read a פסוק as a promise that something will happen.

phrases.english: The Master said: One might think it is a decree.
A decree? From where would that come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: יָכוֹל גְּזֵרָה, גְּזֵרָה מֵהֵיכָא תֵּיתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the "יָכוֹל" (one might think) in the ברייתא of step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What basis is there for reading a פסוק as a fixed decree that something will happen?

steps.title: A precedent: the news that נגעים will come
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds a precedent in the פסוק about נגעי בתים. רבי יהודה reads it as an announcement that נגעים will come. רבי שמעון reads it as excluding נגעי אונסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Yes, we find this. It is written: "And I will place a mark of צרעת in a house of the land of your possession." This is news to them that נגעים will come upon them, says רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: this comes to exclude marks caused by forces beyond one's control.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is a precedent. רבי יהודה reads a פסוק about צרעת on houses as an announcement that it will certainly happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "וְנָתַתִּי נֶגַע צָרַעַת" sound like a promise. רבי יהודה takes it that way: it is news that נגעים will come. רבי שמעון disagrees and uses the פסוק for a halacha: only marks ה׳ places count, not נגעי אונסין.

keyTerms.meaning: News, an announcement of something that will happen
Marks caused by forces beyond one's control

phrases.english: They say: Yes, we find such a thing,
as it is written: "And I will place a mark of צרעת
in a house of the land of your possession"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:34

phrases.english: It is news for them
that נגעים will come upon them,
these are the words of רבי יהודה.
רבי שמעון says:
to exclude marks caused by forces beyond one's control.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 by bringing a precedent.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה reads "וְנָתַתִּי נֶגַע צָרַעַת" as an announcement that נגעים will surely come. So a פסוק can be read as a decree.

steps.title: That is why the פסוק needs "אִם"
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה reads a פסוק as an announcement, one could read the king's פסוק as a decree too. That is why the ברייתא brings the "אִם" of the משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי יהודה say "news"? Here too, one could say it is a decree! Therefore it is written "If."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the precedent back to the ברייתא. Because a פסוק can be read as a sure announcement, the "אִם" was needed to show the king's sin is not decreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's "בְּשׂוֹרָה" shows that the "יָכוֹל גְּזֵרָה" was a real possibility. The "אִם" of the משיח's פסוק blocks that reading for the king.
steps.whatToRemember: "אֲשֶׁר נָשִׂיא יֶחֱטָא" does not mean the king is fated to sin. We might have thought so, as with רבי יהודה's "בְּשׂוֹרָה" about נגעים. The "אִם" of the משיח teaches it only means "if he sins."

phrases.english: Didn't רבי יהודה say "news"?
Here too, I might say it is a decree!
Therefore it is written: "If."
phrases.notes: This is the "אִם" of the משיח's פסוק, which the ברייתא brought in step 20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the precedent of step 22 to the ברייתא of step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The idea of a decree comes from רבי יהודה's reading. The "אִם" of the משיח is brought to show that the king's sin is not decreed.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי שמעון from a ברייתא about נגעים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי שמעון really holds that נגעי אונסין are not טמא. It begins quoting a ברייתא: the laws of נגעים apply "from the statement onward."
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי שמעון, do marks from forces beyond one's control not make a person טמא? But it was taught: "A person, when he will have" means from the statement onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the side point of רבי שמעון's view. It starts quoting a ברייתא that seems to argue with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said נגעי אונסין are not טמא. The ברייתא learns from "אָדָם כִּי יִהְיֶה" only that נגעים which appeared before the command are not טמא. The rest of the ברייתא, in the next lines, will show why this is a problem for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)
From the statement onward (only after ה׳ gave the command)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with רבי שמעון's view is not yet clear from these words alone. The ברייתא is still in the middle of its argument. The point becomes clear in step 26, where it says נגעים are טמא even באונס.

phrases.english: And according to רבי שמעון,
do marks from forces beyond one's control not make a person טמא?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
"A person, when he will have"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:2

phrases.english: from the statement onward.
phrases.notes: Only marks that appear after ה׳ gave this command are טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, נִגְעֵי אוֹנָסִין מִי לָא מְטַמּוּ? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the king and challenges רבי שמעון's view from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that נגעי אונסין are not טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about when the laws of נגעים started will, as it continues, imply that נגעים are טמא even from אונס.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks: can a comparison to זב teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק is needed. A comparison could teach it: just as a זב is טמא only from the command onward, so too נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it a logical argument? The תורה made one טמא through זיבה and made one טמא through נגעים. Just as a זב is only from the statement onward, so too נגעים are only from the statement onward.
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, the ברייתא challenges its own source. It suggests a comparison to זב could teach the same rule. This sets up the ברייתא's next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both זב and נגעים are kinds of טומאה that come from the body. Since זב is טמא only from the command onward, the same could be said of נגעים, and the פסוק of "אָדָם כִּי יִהְיֶה" would not be needed. The ברייתא will need to break this comparison, and that is where the problem for רבי שמעון will show up.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it a logical argument? (why do we need a פסוק)
A man who has a flow that makes him טמא

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical argument:
He made one טמא with זיבה, and He made one טמא with נגעים;
just as a זב is טמא only from the statement onward,
so too נגעים are טמא only from the statement onward?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא דִּין הוּא: טָמֵא בְּזָב וְטָמֵא בִּנְגָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא begun in step 24. The ברייתא asks why its own פסוק is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק "אָדָם כִּי יִהְיֶה" to teach "מִן הַדִּבּוּר וְאֵילָךְ"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison to זב, which is also טמא only from the command onward, should teach the same rule without a פסוק.

steps.title: The comparison to זב does not work
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects learning נגעים from זב, because a זב is not טמא באונס, but נגעים are.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. You can say this about a זב, because a זב does not become טמא when it is caused by outside circumstances. But can you say the same about נגעים, which do make a person טמא even through outside circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the comparison it just made between זב and נגעים. The two are too different to learn one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the ברייתא suggested learning נגעים from זב. Now it points out a difference: a זב caused by אונס is not טמא, but נגעים are טמא even באונס. Since נגעים are 'stricter', you cannot assume the זב rule carries over, so a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Something caused by outside circumstances, not by the person or body on its own
'If you said' — the opening of a rejection of a comparison

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not reject the halacha. It only rejects the way of learning it (the comparison to זב), so the ברייתא will now bring a פסוק instead.

phrases.english: No, if you said this about a זב
that is because he does not become טמא through אונס
phrases.notes: אונס here means something outside caused it, not the body on its own.

phrases.english: will you say the same about נגעים
which do make one טמא even through אונס?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison to זב that was suggested in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison between זב and נגעים, not the halacha itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: זב and נגעים differ: נגעים are טמא even באונס, a זב is not.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches 'from the statement onward'
steps.stepSummary: Because the comparison failed, the ברייתא uses the פסוק 'אדם כי יהיה' to teach that נגעים are טמא only from the command onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the פסוק says: 'When a person shall have' — from the statement onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its proof by bringing the פסוק itself. Along the way it shows that it takes for granted that נגעים are טמא even באונס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the ברייתא that the גמרא quoted in step 24 as a challenge. The ברייתא openly says נגעים are טמא באונס, which seems to go against רבי שמעון from step 22, who read the פסוק as leaving out נגעי אונסין. So the question now is: what does רבי שמעון's פסוק leave out?

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches' — introduces the source that settles the matter
From the time the command was given and onward

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the proof that נגעי אונסין are טמא, which forces the גמרא to reexplain רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Therefore the פסוק says:
"When a person shall have"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:2

phrases.english: from the statement onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא after the comparison was rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נגעים are טמא only from the command onward, and they are טמא even באונס — which challenges רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבא: the פסוק leaves out נגעים from spirits
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי שמעון's exclusion is about נגעים caused by רוחות, not all נגעי אונסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It comes to leave out נגעים caused by spirits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge to רבי שמעון. He narrows what the פסוק leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not leave out every נגע that comes באונס. He only leaves out נגעים caused by רוחות (evil spirits). Ordinary נגעי אונסין are still טמא, so there is no clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To leave out' — this case is excluded

phrases.english: רבא said:
It comes to leave out נגעים caused by spirits.
phrases.notes: He's explaining what רבי שמעון's פסוק (from step 22) really leaves out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that the ברייתא raised against רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון excludes all נגעי אונסין, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון only excludes נגעים from רוחות.

steps.title: רב פפא: the פסוק leaves out נגעים from sorcery
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a different answer: the exclusion is about נגעים caused by כשפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It comes to leave out נגעים caused by sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a second way to answer the same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבא, רב פפא narrows רבי שמעון's exclusion. But for him the case left out is נגעים caused by כשפים (sorcery), not spirits.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
It comes to leave out נגעים caused by sorcery.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: פְּרָט לְנִגְעֵי כְשָׁפִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same challenge, parallel to רבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון excludes all נגעי אונסין.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון only excludes נגעים from כשפים.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves נגעי אונסין are טמא. So רבי שמעון's exclusion is narrowed: רבא says it means נגעים from רוחות, רב פפא says נגעים from כשפים.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a sick נשיא is excluded
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'אשר נשיא יחטא' that a נשיא who is ill is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'When a נשיא sins' — this comes to leave out one who is ill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new topic about the king (נשיא). It quotes a ברייתא that a sick נשיא is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק of the נשיא's חטאת is read as excluding a נשיא who is ill. This is the new teaching the גמרא will now question.

keyTerms.meaning: The king / ruler, who brings a special חטאת

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"When a נשיא sins" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:22

phrases.english: this comes to leave out one who is ill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the נשיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נשיא who is ill is excluded from the law of the נשיא.

steps.title: Does being sick remove a king?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: just because he is sick, does he lose his position as נשיא?
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because he became ill, is he pushed out of his position as נשיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It sounds strange that an ordinary illness would remove someone from being king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implies that a sick נשיא is no longer a נשיא. But a person does not stop being king just because he gets sick. So 'ill' must mean something more specific.

phrases.english: Just because he became ill,
is he pushed out of his position as נשיא?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ חוֹלֶה, אִידְּחִי לֵיהּ מִנְּשִׂיאוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's exclusion of a sick נשיא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Illness alone does not remove someone from being king, so why would he be excluded?

steps.title: It means a נשיא who became a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רב אבדימי בר חמא explains that 'ill' means a נשיא who became a מצורע, and proves it from King עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אבדימי בר חמא said: It leaves out a נשיא who became a מצורע, as it says: 'And ה׳ struck the king, and he was a מצורע until the day of his death, and he lived in a house of freedom, and יותם the king's son was over the household.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אבדימי בר חמא answers the challenge. The 'illness' is צרעת, and a פסוק shows that a king with צרעת stopped ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every sickness removes a king, but צרעת does. The פסוק shows that once the king became a מצורע, he lived apart and his son יותם took over. So he really was no longer the ruling נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'house of freedom' — a separate house where he lived
In charge of the household / the palace

phrases.english: רב אבדימי בר חמא said:
It leaves out a נשיא who became a מצורע,
as it says:
"And ה׳ struck the king,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 15:5. The king here is עזריה.

phrases.english: and he was a מצורע until the day of his death,
and he lived in a house of freedom,
and יותם, the king's son, was over the household."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַבְדִּימִי בַּר חָמָא: פְּרָט לְנָשִׂיא שֶׁנִּצְטָרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 31 by defining 'ill' as צרעת.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any sick נשיא loses his position, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a נשיא who became a מצורע is removed, as we see with King עזריה.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Ill' in the ברייתא means a מצורע. A king with צרעת stops ruling, as the פסוק about עזריה and his son יותם shows.

steps.title: Until then, the king was a servant
steps.stepSummary: From 'house of freedom' the גמרא learns that while he ruled, the king was really a servant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק says 'in a house of freedom', we learn that until now he was a servant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a side comment on the words 'בית החפשית'. If he only now became 'free', then while he was king he was not free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling his new home a 'house of freedom' implies that being king was a kind of servitude. A leader serves the people; he is not just their master. This idea sets up the story that comes next.

phrases.english: Since the פסוק says "in a house of freedom,"
this implies that until now
he was a servant.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר בְּבֵית הַחׇפְשִׁית, מִכְּלָל דְּעַד הַשְׁתָּא עֶבֶד הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side lesson drawn from a word in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person in a position of leadership is really a servant of the people.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea — leadership is servitude — is the theme that the following story about רבן גמליאל is connected to.

steps.title: Setting up the story: the ship journey
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע travel by ship. רבן גמליאל brought only bread, but רבי יהושע brought bread and flour, and רבן גמליאל ends up relying on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע, who were traveling on a ship. רבן גמליאל had bread with him. רבי יהושע had bread and flour. רבן גמליאל's bread ran out, and he relied on רבי יהושע's flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to the idea of leaders as servants. This step sets the scene for the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trip took longer than expected. רבי יהושע had planned ahead with extra flour, and רבן גמליאל had to use it. This sets up רבן גמליאל's question about how רבי יהושע knew to bring it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like this story of' — introduces a story

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Like this story of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע,
who were traveling on a ship.
רבן גמליאל had bread with him;

phrases.aramaic: בַּהֲדֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הֲוָה פִּיתָּא וְסוּלְתָּא.
phrases.english: רבי יהושע had bread and flour with him.
רבן גמליאל's bread ran out,
and he relied on רבי יהושע's flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הֲווֹ אָזְלִי בִּסְפִינְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story connected to the idea that leadership is servitude.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: רבי יהושע planned ahead and brought extra flour.

steps.title: Did you know there would be a delay?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל asks רבי יהושע whether he knew in advance the trip would take so long.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did you know that we would have such a long delay, that you brought flour?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל asks how רבי יהושע knew to pack extra food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing flour, not just bread, shows רבי יהושע expected a long trip. רבן גמליאל wants to know what he knew.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל is speaking to רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Did you know
that we would have such a long delay
that you brought flour?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי הֲוָה יָדְעַתְּ דְּהָוֵה לַן עִכּוּבָא כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The question arising from the story's setup.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יהושע knew the trip would be long.

steps.title: The star that misleads sailors
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע explains that a certain star rises once in seventy years and leads sailors off course, so he prepared in case it rose.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is one star that rises once in seventy years and leads the sailors astray. I said: Maybe it will rise and lead us astray.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers that his knowledge of the stars made him prepare for a possible delay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not know for sure. He knew a rare star could appear and mislead sailors, so he brought extra flour just in case. This shows his great wisdom.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There is one star that, once in seventy years,
rises and leads the sailors astray.
phrases.notes: The printed גמרא says 'ships' in round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets says 'sailors'.

phrases.english: And I said:
Maybe it will rise and lead us astray.
phrases.notes: The word 'us' in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹכָב אֶחָד לְשִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה עוֹלֶה וּמַתְעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rare star might rise and mislead them, so he prepared extra food.

steps.title: So wise, yet working on a ship?
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל is surprised that someone so wise has to travel by ship to make a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have so much wisdom, and you go on a ship?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל wonders why such a wise man has to take hard, risky trips to earn money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל sees that רבי יהושע is extremely wise. He is surprised that such a person does not have an easier way to support himself.

keyTerms.meaning: You have so much (wisdom) in your hand

phrases.english: He said to him:
You have so much wisdom,
phrases.notes: Literally 'so much is in your hand'; he means so much knowledge.

phrases.english: and you go on a ship?

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל כָּךְ בְּיָדְךָ, וְאַתָּה עוֹלֶה בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the wisdom רבי יהושע just showed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why such a wise man must travel by ship for a living.

steps.title: Wonder instead about your two poor students
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע points to two brilliant students, רבי אלעזר חסמא and רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא, who have no food or clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Before you wonder about me, wonder about two students you have on land, רבי אלעזר חסמא and רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא. They know how to calculate how many drops are in the sea, yet they have no bread to eat and no clothes to wear!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע turns the question around. If you are surprised about me, look at your two students who are even worse off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These students are so brilliant they can calculate the drops in the sea. Yet they are terribly poor. רבי יהושע is hinting that רבן גמליאל, as the leader, should do something for them.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Before you wonder about me,
wonder about two students
that you have on dry land:
רבי אלעזר חסמא
and רבי יוחנן בן גודגדא,
who know how to calculate
how many drops there are in the sea,
and they have no bread to eat
and no clothes to wear!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁאַתָּה תָּמֵהַּ עָלַי, תְּמַהּ עַל שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל by pointing to an even more surprising case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two brilliant students live in poverty on land; that should surprise you more.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל decides to appoint them
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל makes up his mind to seat the two students at the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: He made up his mind to seat them at the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its result: רבן גמליאל decides to give the two students positions of leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל took רבי יהושע's hint. He planned to give the poor scholars important positions, which would also give them a livelihood. This connects back to leadership, the topic that brought the story in.

keyTerms.meaning: To seat them at the head (give them leadership positions)

phrases.english: He made up his mind to seat them at the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל's response to רבי יהושע's words.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן גמליאל decided to appoint the two poor scholars to positions of leadership.
steps.whatToRemember: A king with צרעת leaves his throne and moves to a 'house of freedom', showing that ruling is a kind of servitude. The story of רבן גמליאל appointing two poor scholars is brought in connection with that idea.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל sends for the two scholars twice
steps.stepSummary: When רבן גמליאל came ashore, he sent for the two scholars. They did not come the first time but came the second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came up from the ship, he sent for them, and they did not come. He sent for them again, and they came.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. רבן גמליאל acts on the decision he made on the ship and calls the two scholars, who come only after the second call.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 39 רבן גמליאל decided to seat the two students at the head. Here he carries out that decision. The text does not say why they ignored the first call, but his words in the next step suggest how he understood it.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came up (from the ship onto dry land)

phrases.english: When he came up,
phrases.notes: He means when רבן גמליאל got off the ship and came up onto land.

phrases.english: he sent for them, and they did not come;
he sent again, and they came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the decision from Step 39 to seat the two scholars at the head.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל called the scholars twice, and they came only the second time.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל asks if they think he is giving them power
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל asks the scholars whether they imagine he is handing them authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Do you think that I am giving you power and authority?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל speaks to the two scholars with a pointed question. This line sets up his next statement about what the appointment really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question challenges the idea that a leadership post is mainly honor and power. Because they came only on the second call, he responds by asking how they view the appointment. His answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you imagine / do you think

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real request for information. רבן גמליאל is asking a pointed question to correct how they see the appointment. He is not offering them a title of glory.

phrases.english: He said to them: Do you imagine
that I am giving you authority?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: כִּמְדוּמִּין אַתֶּם שֶׁשְּׂרָרָה אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the scholars coming only on the second call in Step 40.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל challenges the idea that the appointment he is offering is a grant of power.
